events.verdict: LaVine (SAC) initiates body contact with George's (UTA) body as he is airborne, which affects his body's trajectory and shot attempt near the rim.
Filipowski (UTA) moves alongside Schroder's (SAC) path and maintains a legal guarding position as incidental contact occurs during the driving shot attempt.
Schroder (SAC) reaches toward the ball when marginal contact occurs with Markkanen (UTA), who moves through the contact into the lane.
Markkanen (UTA) maintains a legal guarding position and incidental contact occurs as he defends LaVine (SAC) during the drive.
Westbrook (SAC) maintains verticality and absorbs the contact that occurs during George's (UTA) driving shot attempt.
George (UTA) establishes himself in a legal guarding position in LaVine's (SAC) path and absorbs the contact in his chest as LaVine drives through his space.
Westbrook (SAC) initiates contact with Markkanen's (UTA) arm and the contact affects his ability to maintain control the ball.
Westbrook (SAC) steps into the paint prior to the release of Markkanen's (UTA) free throw attempt. A lane violation is correctly called.
LaVine (SAC) is already in Clayton Jr.'s (UTA) path when contact occurs, and he absorbs the contact during the screen.
George (UTA) is moving alongside LaVine's (SAC) path and absorbs the marginal contact that occurs during the drive.
George (UTA) cleanly dislodges the ball prior to incidental contact occurring between Clayton Jr. (UTA) and DeRozan (SAC) as they come together in the lane.
Kessler (UTA) bobbles the rebound when marginal contact occurs for Sabonis (SAC), who is reaching for the loose ball.
Kessler (UTA) initiates contact with Sabonis' (SAC) arm, which affects his play at the basket.
Markkanen (UTA) firms up over his left foot when marginal contact occurs with LaVine (SAC) during the off-ball screen.
Schroder (SAC) legally contests George's (UTA) jump shot attempt.
